title: Ion channel drugs can make planarian head number flip stochastically at each regeneration

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Ion channel drugs can make planarian head number flip stochastically at each regeneration

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Exposure to ion channel drugs can put the planarian bioelectric circuit into a bistable state in which, at each regeneration, fragments of these 'cryptic' worms randomly regenerate as one-headed or two-headed, analogous to bistability in perceptual systems.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Reprogrammability, external manipulation, and representation

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Exposure to ion channel drugs (a physiological experience akin to electrical signals from a retina or other sense organ, not a genetic change) can place the bioelectric circuit into a state in which it cannot decide between two outcomes and flips back and forth stochastically at each regenerative event (recall of target morphology).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind”, Animal cognition (2023), doi:10.1007/s10071-023-01780-3; section “Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Reprogrammability, external manipulation, and representation”. Scope: Planarian flatworms treated with ion channel or gap-junction drugs (Durant et al. 2017)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-glue-14: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Repeated head-number transitions are direct, quantifiable outcomes with clear controls. Existing published observations can test switching, but inferring a bistable bioelectric circuit rather than hidden heterogeneity requires matched physiological measurements.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Track identified treated worms and their fragments over repeated regeneration rounds, estimate transition probabilities between one- and two-head outcomes, and compare them with fixed-state and untreated controls. A reproducible nonzero switching process without further drug exposure confirms bistable or stochastic phenotype switching.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Apparent randomness may reflect unmeasured physiological state.

Raw longitudinal lineage records may not be public.

Stochastic switching does not uniquely establish circuit bistability.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.52
data existence: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.78
analysis feasibility: 0.82
operationalizability: 0.95

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Stochastic one-head versus two-head outcomes across rounds are countable, and the cryptic-worm experiments report that mixture after a physiological treatment. The lineage sequences needed to separate true flipping from a mixture of stable animals are not deposited. Existing published proportions therefore test the result only in part.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For fragments from ion-channel-drug-treated cryptic worms, record head number at each successive regeneration without further drug and test whether the two outcomes occur as draws rather than as a fixed lineage state. Frequencies near a stable mixture, with individual lines flipping, would support bistable recall; each fragment locking to one morphology, or flipping only while the drug remains, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Per-fragment outcome sequences are not a public table, so published proportions could hide stable subclasses.

Environmental noise between cuts can imitate a bistable circuit.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.45
